questions: Should the random seed be set inside the function (e.g., seed(42)) to ensure reproducible results across calls, or is randomness intended to be fresh each time?
Are the elements within each sublist (e.g., numbers 1, 2) relevant for the selection process, or are they only used to determine the length (i.e., their values are ignored)?
If a sublist is empty, should the corresponding Counter be empty (i.e., Counter()) or should it be omitted from the output list?
Is the choice of items weighted uniformly across POSSIBLE_ITEMS, or could there be a non-uniform distribution (e.g., some items more likely)?
Should the function modify the input list_of_lists in any way, or is it purely read-only?
What should happen if list_of_lists contains non-list elements (e.g., a string or integer) instead of sublists?
Is the order of Counters in the output list required to match the order of sublists in list_of_lists exactly?
Should the function handle the case where POSSIBLE_ITEMS is an empty list, and if so, what should happen when a selection is attempted?
